opening_message:
Ticket 1: Maurice Perez (employee ID E036) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E036.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Maurice Perez (E036) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access, and the role owns the system, so write is within policy. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check for Maurice Perez (E036): record shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training (never admin). The requested write access exceeds the maximum for a basic-trained contractor, so the maximum is read. Recommend granting read to Source Code.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists Maurice Perez (E036) as full-time, while Security's record check lists contractor with basic security training. Under policy, a contractor with only basic training may have at most read access to Source Code (write requires advanced training; never admin). Since the requested write exceeds that maximum, granting the maximum of read is the appropriate, policy-compliant decision based on the security record.
